cards.heading: Transformer: definition
cards.question: What is the Transformer architecture?
cards.answer: A sequence transduction architecture that dispenses with recurrence and convolution entirely, relying solely on attention: self-attention layers relate every position in a sequence to every other position directly, in an encoder-decoder configuration.

cards.heading: Transformer vs recurrence: path length
cards.question: How does the path length between any two tokens differ between a Transformer and a recurrent model?
cards.answer: Constant-length in a Transformer, since every layer attends over all positions at once; under recurrence it takes one step per position, since position t cannot be processed until t-1.

cards.heading: Why Transformers parallelize training
cards.question: Why does removing recurrence let Transformer training parallelize across sequence positions?
cards.answer: Recurrence imposes a sequential dependency (t depends on t-1) that blocks parallelization within a training example; attending over the whole sequence at once removes that dependency, so the whole sequence computes in parallel on accelerators.

cards.heading: The Transformer's core trade-off
cards.question: What trade-off does the Transformer make in exchange for training parallelism and shorter dependency paths?
cards.answer: It pays attention's quadratic cost in sequence length — the architectural decision underneath essentially every modern large language model.

cards.heading: Transformer: original benchmark evidence
cards.question: What machine translation results did the original 2017 Transformer paper report?
cards.answer: 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German (over 2 BLEU past prior ensembles) and 41.8 BLEU single-model state of the art on English-to-French, trained in 3.5 days on eight GPUs.

cards.heading: Transformer: generalization beyond translation
cards.question: What did the original paper show beyond machine translation, and what did the architecture become?
cards.answer: Successful transfer to English constituency parsing, within the paper itself — and the architecture went on to become the substrate of modern large language models.
